lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 22: troubleshooting Services, DNS, stuck deletes and sick nodes
lesson.shortTitle: Troubleshooting Services, DNS, deletes and nodes
lesson.description: Fix a Service with no endpoints, a DNS lookup that fails, an object stuck in Terminating, a NotReady node and an evicted Pod, then debug with kubectl debug.
lesson.tested: Broke and fixed each case on a two-node kind v0.33.0 cluster, node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Most failures outside the Pod are a mismatch you can read from the API: a selector with no endpoints, a name in the wrong namespace, a finalizer nobody owns, or a node that stopped reporting.

cheatsheet.intro: Services, DNS, stuck deletes, sick nodes, and the commands from Lesson 22.

rows.name: Service name, endpoints, port, Pod
rows.role: Follow a Service request in that order. bad address and Connection refused point at different stops.
rows.where: kubectl get endpointslices, then exec and wget or netstat

rows.name: DNS
rows.role: If CoreDNS is scaled to zero, lookups fail until you scale it back. /etc/resolv.conf in the Pod shows the cluster DNS.

rows.name: Finalizer
rows.role: Keeps an object, or a whole namespace, in Terminating until its owner removes the finalizer. The namespace conditions tell you which one.

rows.name: Silent node
rows.role: In the lab the node was NotReady after about 50 seconds, lost Service traffic at once, and lost its Pods after the 300-second default toleration.

rows.name: Eviction
rows.role: The kubelet evicts Pods to protect its node. status.reason tells you when that happened. The kubelet does not respect a PDB for node-pressure eviction.

rows.name: kubectl debug
rows.role: Adds tools next to a shell-less container (--target) or on a node (node/<name>, then chroot /host).

rows.name: See Service endpoints
rows.where: empty set means the selector matches no Pod

rows.name: Clear a stuck finalizer
rows.where: only when you understand why it is there

rows.name: Debug a node
rows.where: sees the node's systemd and disks

items.what: Follow the request in order: name, endpoints, port, Pod. Connection refused and bad address are different stops.
Stopping kubelet made the worker NotReady. Replacements stayed Pending with an untolerated taint until kubelet started again.
status.reason said Evicted: Pod ephemeral local storage usage exceeds the total limit of containers 20Mi. Failed Pods stay until you delete them.
kubectl debug node/k8s-ep22-worker ran chroot /host. On kind that worked. The docs say it fails without privilege, and the lesson points at --profile=sysadmin.

commands.note: empty means the selector matches nothing
compare the selector with pod labels

commands.cmd: kubectl exec -n k8s-from-zero client -- nslookup web.k8s-from-zero.svc.cluster.local
kubectl get configmap stuck -n k8s-from-zero -o jsonpath='{.metadata.deletionTimestamp}{"  "}{.metadata.finalizers}{"\n"}'
kubectl get pod disk-hog -n k8s-from-zero -o jsonpath='{.status.phase} {.status.reason}: {.status.message}{"\n"}'

kubectl debug node/k8s-ep22-worker -n k8s-from-zero --image=busybox:1.37 -- chroot /host sh -c 'systemctl is-active kubelet containerd; df -h /var | tail -1; journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager -n 3 -o cat | cut -c1-110'

homework.intro: The lesson uses a two-node kind cluster (lab name k8s-ep22) and the namespace k8s-from-zero. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: In what order should you follow a failing Service request, and what do bad address and Connection refused point at?
exercises.a: Name, endpoints, port, Pod. bad address points earlier (often DNS or the name). Connection refused points later: the packet arrived but nothing is listening on that port, for example a wrong targetPort.

exercises.q: What does a finalizer do, and how do you see which one is blocking a namespace?
exercises.a: It keeps the object, or a whole namespace, in Terminating until its owner removes that key from metadata.finalizers. Namespace conditions tell you which object still has a finalizer. The docs warn not to strip a finalizer unless you understand it and have cleaned up another way.

exercises.q: What did the lab observe when kubelet was stopped on a worker, and when does node-pressure eviction happen?
exercises.a: The node became NotReady after about 50 seconds, lost Service traffic at once, and lost its Pods after the 300-second default toleration. Node-pressure eviction is the kubelet terminating Pods to reclaim node resources; status.reason records it, and a PDB is not respected.

exercises.q: The web Service has no endpoints. What two mismatches does the lesson fix, in order?
exercises.a: First a wrong selector, patched to app.kubernetes.io/name=web so EndpointSlices fill. Then a wrong targetPort, found with netstat inside the Pod and patched so traffic hits the listening port.

exercises.q: You scale CoreDNS to zero, then back to two. What fails in between?
exercises.a: DNS lookups from a client Pod fail until CoreDNS is running again. /etc/resolv.conf in the Pod still points at the cluster DNS Service.

exercises.q: How do you get a shell in the pause Pod, and how do you inspect kubelet on the node?
exercises.a: kubectl debug -it --image=busybox:1.37 --target=app -c shell for the shell-less Pod. kubectl debug node/<name> --image=busybox:1.37 -- chroot /host sh, then systemctl and df, for the node.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: A namespace stays Terminating after you deleted its last app. Where do you look first?
exercises.a: The namespace status conditions, and objects in that namespace that still have metadata.finalizers. A finalizer on a ConfigMap in the lab was enough to hold the namespace.

exercises.q: A Pod is Failed and status.reason mentions eviction or disk pressure. Did drain do this?
exercises.a: Not necessarily. The kubelet can evict Pods itself under node pressure, without kubectl drain, and it does not honour a PDB in that case.
